boundary_rationale: The span's front seam, at Lam.3.60/Lam.3.61, rests on the acrostic letter change from resh to shin, and no accompanying voice, addressee or topic shift falls at either verse; the direct address to YHWH about the enemies' hostility continues across that seam without a content break, disclosed here as part of this span's own confidence assessment. The shin and tav triplets (3:61-63, 3:64-66) close the whole triple acrostic, reporting the enemies' plotting under direct address to YHWH through 3:61-3:63, the shin triplet's one true imperative anchored at הַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.3.63, byte tier) amid its closing report clauses, before turning, in the tav triplet, to three verse-initial second-masculine-singular prefix-conjugation verbs of prospective retribution against them, each verse-initial in the same construction (sweep: 3 verses): תָּשִׁ֨יב לָהֶ֥ם גְּמ֛וּל יְהוָ֖ה כְּמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְדֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Lam.3.64, byte tier), תִּתֵּ֤ן לָהֶם֙ מְגִנַּת לֵ֔ב תַּאֲלָֽתְךָ֖ לָהֶֽם (oshb:Lam.3.65, byte tier) and תִּרְדֹּ֤ף בְּאַף֙ וְתַשְׁמִידֵ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת שְׁמֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Lam.3.66, byte tier); the WEB witness renders the opening verb “You will pay them back, Yahweh, according to the work of their hands.” (web:Lam.3.64) and the closing verb, at the poem's own final verse, “You will pursue them in anger, and destroy them from under the heavens of Yahweh.” (web:Lam.3.66). This closing shift from report to prospective retribution is the disclosed reason the span is not extended further back into the qof/resh material; it is an operative-category deviation from a plain unit_type label, disclosed here rather than left silent.

In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save.” (web:Lam.4.17). Whether this turn belongs fully to 4:17 or is already anticipated in 4:16's account of favor withheld is held open rather than decided; the seam is drawn at the acrostic's own ayin line since that is where the plural 'our' enters the verse text (first-plural suffix tokens: 0 of this poem's first 16 verses carry one, and 15 stand across 4:17-4:20, with a further first-plural element, the prefix-conjugation נִֽחְיֶ֥ה at Lam.4.20, standing outside that suffix census). boundary_rationale: The fifth poem opens without an acrostic but with a three-imperative chain: זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier) is followed in the same verse by a ketiv-qere pair, הביט הַבִּ֖יטָה (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier; the inventory's own K/Q note here), both readings meaning look or regard, and then by a third imperative carrying its own vav prefix, וּרְאֵ֥ה (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier); the full verse, זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙ מֶֽה הָ֣יָה לָ֔נוּ הביט הַבִּ֖יטָה וּרְאֵ֥ה אֶת חֶרְפָּתֵֽנוּ (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier), reads “Remember, Yahweh, what has come on us. Look, and see our reproach.” (web:Lam.5.1). As a petition imperative to the divine name, the remember-form stands in 2 verses, here and at web:Lam.3.19 (skeleton tier), the third member of its 3-verse bare-token census being the negated third-person perfect at web:Lam.2.1; the look-form stands in 2 verses as a bare token and in 4 under the single-letter prefix test, at web:Lam.1.11, web:Lam.2.20, web:Lam.3.63 and web:Lam.5.1 (skeleton tier at both digits). The communal voice then catalogs loss across 5:2-5:10 without a further direct address to YHWH: inheritance surrendered, “We are orphans and fatherless. Our mothers are as widows.” (web:Lam.5.3), water and wood bought at a price, foreign servitude, inherited guilt, and at the group's own close, עוֹרֵ֨נוּ֙ כְּתַנּ֣וּר נִכְמָ֔רוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י זַלְעֲפ֥וֹת רָעָֽב (oshb:Lam.5.10, byte tier), “Our skin is black like an oven, because of the burning heat of famine.” (web:Lam.5.10) — the catalogue's 1st-plural form closing before a four-verse gap at Lam.5.11-Lam.5.14 (1st-plural sweep: 0 of those 4 verses), where a run of third-plural verbs on bare plural human-group subjects opens at 5:11.

boundary_rationale: This group opens on its own texture rather than continuing what precedes it: 5:11 through 5:14 (4 verses) each open with a bare plural human-group noun followed by a third-plural verb — נָשִׁים֙ בְּצִיּ֣וֹן עִנּ֔וּ בְּתֻלֹ֖ת בְּעָרֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Lam.5.11, byte tier), “They ravished the women in Zion, the virgins in the cities of Judah.” (web:Lam.5.11); שָׂרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.12, byte tier); בַּחוּרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.13, byte tier); and זְקֵנִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.14, byte tier) — none of the four carrying a 1st-plural form, against the 1st-plural catalogue that runs unbroken through the verse immediately in front of this span, web:Lam.5.10 (1st-plural sweep: 10 of 10 verses, Lam.5.1-Lam.5.10). The catalog continues from economic loss into social and personal violation: “The young men carry millstones. The children stumbled under loads of wood.” (web:Lam.5.13), princes hanged, elders gone from the gate. The group turns from external causes to the community's own confession, נָֽפְלָה֙ עֲטֶ֣רֶת רֹאשֵׁ֔נוּ — the crown fallen from our head (oshb:Lam.5.16, byte tier) — “The crown has fallen from our head.” (web:Lam.5.16), the sixth of this span's eight verses. It closes on the desolation named directly, הַר צִיּוֹן֙ שֶׁשָּׁמֵ֔ם (oshb:Lam.5.18, byte tier), “the mountain of Zion, which is desolate” (web:Lam.5.18); the verse also carries this poem's only parashah mark, tier-3 weak and single-witness (the PE type marks 1 verse here; the samekh type marks 0 verses in this poem, the two never conflated), corroborating a close already carried by the discourse turn to direct address that follows at web:Lam.5.19 rather than driving it.

boundary_rationale: The poem turns from catalog to hymn: אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְעוֹלָ֣ם תֵּשֵׁ֔ב כִּסְאֲךָ֖ לְדֹ֥ר וָדֽוֹר (oshb:Lam.5.19, byte tier) reopens direct address to YHWH after the descriptive verses behind it, “You, Yahweh, remain forever. The petition, הֲשִׁיבֵ֨נוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ ונשוב וְֽנָשׁ֔וּבָה (oshb:Lam.5.21, byte tier; the inventory's own K/Q note here, ketiv/qere ונשוב / וְֽנָשׁ֔וּבָה, both readings meaning turn or return), “Turn us to yourself, Yahweh, and we will be turned.” (web:Lam.5.21). Whether 5:19-5:22 forms a close of its own or reads on from the petition before it is held open rather than decided; the poem's closing word stays unresolved, “you have utterly rejected us” (web:Lam.5.22).
